groups.title: State from the server
groups.text: Alpine lives in the HTML PAD writes. Its state comes from the page's PHP as JSON in the attribute - the ^ sigil writes it - or as the argument of a component registered in a file of www/.

groups.title: Talking back to PAD
groups.text: A component asks the page again: the JSON of $padExpose, a post with the session's token, a stream of events. The server keeps the truth.

examples.title: State from PHP
examples.lede: x-data="{^profile}": the page's PHP prepares an array, the ^ sigil writes it as JSON into the attribute, and Alpine makes it live - no braces of Alpine's in the template at all.

examples.title: Components in a file
examples.lede: Tabs, an accordion and a dialog registered with Alpine.data in www/alpine/ - the template calls them by name and hands them PAD's data as the argument: x-data="accordion({^faq})".

examples.title: Live search
examples.lede: x-model.debounce feeds a fetch of the same page with padFormat=json; the PHP that rendered the first results answers the next ones as JSON - $padExpose names what may leave.

examples.title: One set of rules
examples.lede: The rules live in the page's PHP: padValidate checks the post with them, padValidateClient hands them to Alpine, and {validator} checks them in the browser first - the same messages on both sides.

examples.title: A list PAD keeps
examples.lede: Every change shows at once and is posted to the page, which keeps the list in the session and answers it - the server's answer is the list. Reload, and it is still there.

examples.title: Server-sent events
examples.lede: padSse sends the server's numbers every second as JSON; the component opens an EventSource in x-init and closes it when the stream says it is done.
